newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbeks to privatise molybdenum-tungsten combine.
newsitem.headline: Uzbeks to privatise molybdenum-tungsten combine.

text.p: Uzbekistan's refractory and heatproof alloy plant will be privatised in the third quarter of the year, in line with a government decision, an industry source said on Friday.
Oleg Ivanov, deputy director general of Uzbekistan's state concern Spetssplav (Special Alloy) told Reuters the planned sell-off was likely to replenish the combine's scarce finances.

The company -- built in 1956 near the town of Chirchik in north-eastern Uzbekistan to produce alloys, powders and rolling from molybdenum and tungsten -- needs at least $10 million of circulating capital, he said.

Ivanov said the fixed assets of the combine were worth one billion sums, or around $17 million, taking into account the officially set rate of 60 sums per dollar. The market rate offered nationwide by street dealers is 150 sums to the dollar.
The final analysis of the assets and the privatisation mechanism will be completed within the next two months.

Ivanov declined to provide figures on the combine's output, but said the company was working at only 35 percent of its installed capacity. The plunge in output was due to lower deliveries of molybdenum and tungsten concentrates from Russia, he said.

Uzbek molybdenum and tungsten ores traditionally account for 40 percent of the raw materials processed by the combine. The remaining 60 percent is imported from Russia and Mongolia. --Shamil Baigin, Tashkent Newsroom, +7 3712 361958
